newsitem.title: UK: RESEARCH ALERT-NatWest cut at Lehman. [CORRECTED 15:20 GMT]
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-NatWest cut at Lehman. [CORRECTED 15:20 GMT]

text.p: National Westminster Bank Plc was cut to "underperform" from "outperform" by Lehman Brothers, the investment bank said on Tuesday.
Lehman analyst Robert Law said he cut his pre-tax profit forecast for NatWest by 13 percent to 1,750 million stg for the current year and expected the dividend to be held at last year's level.
(Corrects forecast for NatWest from 2,000 million stg to 1,750 million stg.)
On Monday NatWest issued a profit warning and announced a review of its investment banking operations, along with the departure of NatWest Markets head Martin Owen.

"It is difficult to escape the conclusion that NatWest has no obviously sizeable businesses with attractive profitability, market share or competitive advantage," Law said. "It is unclear how even the most radical action can transform the prospects for the group."
"It is encouraging that at last the group appears to see the value in increasing the resources in the retail area," the Lehman analyst said.

"However the repositioning undertaken over the past year went in precisely the opposite direction, and with the Bancorp proceeds now spent, NatWest appears to have limited room to reverse this process."
